fields.default: Island roads, rooftop sunsets and a change of plans. My Philippines adventure with friends became a story I could never have planned.

fields.label: The journey took us through Cebu, Oslob, Panglao and Bohol, Boracay, El Nido and Manila. Getting bet
fields.default: The journey took us through Cebu, Oslob, Panglao and Bohol, Boracay, El Nido and Manila. Getting between those places was part of the experience: buses, boats, flights and the public bus from El Nido to Puerto Princesa. The photographs show the views, but they are only one part of what travelling together felt like.

fields.label: El Nido brought a villa, scooters, the zipline and evenings at Amigos. Then a typhoon changed the ro
fields.default: El Nido brought a villa, scooters, the zipline and evenings at Amigos. Then a typhoon changed the route. We had wanted to continue to Moalboal and other islands; instead, we were unable to move on as planned. After so much activity, that pause was frustrating. We eventually travelled through Puerto Princesa and flew to Manila for the last part of the holiday.

fields.label: I do not want to edit that difficult part out of the memory just because the coastline looked beauti
fields.default: I do not want to edit that difficult part out of the memory just because the coastline looked beautiful. The trip was busy, funny, occasionally uncomfortable and very different from the simple bucket-list idea I had started with. Rooftop sunsets belong in the story, but so do nervous flights and plans that did not survive the weather.

fields.default: This note is the short reflection. The full Philippines story follows the route in chapters, with my photographs and films beside the places and moments they belong to. It is a record of our 2025 trip, rather than advice that the same route will work in the same way today.
